faqs.question: What is the best Veo alternative for grassroots football?
faqs.answer: The best Veo alternative for grassroots football is the option that gives teams useful match output without adding heavy equipment. Pitchside AI is being built for that exact problem: turning one phone recording into player stats, highlights and match clips. For 5-a-side, futsal and Sunday league teams, this is often more practical than buying a dedicated camera system.

Veo is camera-first: it helps teams capture full-match footage using dedicated camera hardware. Pitchside AI is player-output-first: it is being built to turn normal phone footage into goals, assists, saves, highlights and useful grassroots football stats. That makes Pitchside better suited to teams that care more about clips and proof of performance than full tactical video.

faqs.question: How should we record matches for Pitchside AI?
faqs.answer: The best starting point is simple: record the match on a phone from a stable angle where most of the pitch is visible. For small-sided games, one corner or halfway-side angle can often capture enough action. The goal is not broadcast footage; it is usable match footage that can later become stats, clips and player moments.

contentBlocks.content: Why a Camera Alone Is Not Enough for Grassroots Football

For funded clubs, a dedicated camera can make sense. Coaches may need full-pitch shape, pressing structure, off-ball movement and team-wide tactical review. But grassroots football has a different problem. Most teams do not fail because they lack a camera. They fail because the footage they already capture never becomes useful.

That is the gap Pitchside AI is designed to fill. If a player records the match on a phone, the next step should not be a forgotten video file. The next step should be player stats, highlights, saves, goals, assists and moments worth sharing.

sections.content:
Veo built grassroots filming into a category. A self-following AI camera on a tripod, a club subscription, and suddenly Sunday league teams had panoramic match footage. For well-funded clubs, it works.

But most grassroots football isn't well-funded. It's a 5-a-side team that books a pitch on Thursdays, a Sunday league side splitting subs, a uni team with no kit budget. For them, a Veo setup raises three hard questions: Who pays for the camera? Who carries and mounts it every week? Who edits the two-hour recording into something worth watching?

That's the gap a real Veo alternative has to close — not just "cheaper hardware," but no hardware to own, mount, or operate at all.

This page breaks down what Veo actually costs, what a genuine alternative needs to do, and how phone-based capture compares to both Veo cameras and GPS tracker vests.
sections.heading: Introduction

definitionBox.text: Veo is an AI-powered sports camera that records full matches from a fixed tripod and auto-generates highlights. A Veo alternative is any system that captures match footage, stats, or highlights without Veo's dedicated camera hardware — most commonly a phone-based app or a manual recording setup.

sections.heading: What is Veo, and why look for an alternative?
sections.content:
People search for a Veo alternative for four recurring reasons:

• Cost — the camera plus subscription is out of reach for casual teams.
• Logistics — someone has to own, transport, mount, and charge the unit every single week.
• Format — Veo is built around full-pitch club football, not 5-a-side or futsal.
• Lock-in — footage and features sit behind an ongoing club subscription.

If any of those apply to you, you're not looking for a better camera. You're looking for a way to skip the camera.

sections.heading: The real cost of a Veo camera in 2026

callout.text: The biggest cost of a Veo camera isn't the price tag — it's the recurring commitment. Every match needs someone to own the gear, set it up, and process the footage afterward.

sections.content:
The sticker price isn't the whole story. The honest cost of a fixed-camera setup stacks up across four layers:

• Hardware — a dedicated AI camera unit (historically four figures to buy outright).
• Subscription — ongoing club/season fees to unlock editing and storage.
• Setup labour — someone arrives early every match to mount and align the tripod.
• Editing time — raw footage still needs trimming into shareable clips.
sections.disclaimer: Pricing for camera systems changes frequently — always confirm current figures with the vendor before budgeting.

sections.content: A phone-based app is the only category that can realistically hit all seven, because the camera is already in everyone's pocket.

• "Highlights have to be edited manually." Manual editing is the old way. Automatic, footage-based highlight generation is exactly what newer tools are being built to handle.
